inputs.sbc_source: Post-spin continuing-ops run-rate: FY2025 cash-flow add-back 116.8 (10-K FY2025, whole company incl. Ralliant H1 and a 50.9 Q3-2025 spin-related step-up) is not the base; Q4-2025 19.9 + Q1-2026 21.3 + Q2-2026 23.9 (10-Q 2026-07-03, ShareBasedCompensation YTD 45.2) annualise to ~90, plus ~5 of net-share-settlement withholding (last tagged 17.0 in FY2021 for the pre-spin company) = 95. Combined figure not published; the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow 1,610.1 (part-funded by the 1,146.8 Ralliant separation proceeds); H1-2026 a further 700.3. The company is an active repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention. Buybacks are value-neutral here: SBC is fully expensed and the count held flat.
inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page shares outstanding 302.0M at 2026-07-24 (10-Q filed 2026-07-29) plus 3.4M incremental dilutive shares from the Q2-2026 diluted-EPS table = 305.4M fully diluted. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the 313.4M FY2025 year-end and 334.6M FY2025 weighted-average counts in the CSV are stale after 700.3 of H1-2026 repurchases.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 (diversified industrial with ~50% recurring revenue) -> cost of equity ~9.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (10-Q fair value of term debt 3,432.8 vs carrying 3,509.3; FY2025 periodic interest 145 on ~3.3B), ~4.0% after tax. Weights ~83% equity (17.1B market cap) / 17% debt (3.5B) -> 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the driver paths and the weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842) are expensed inside EBITDA through opex; the 88.8 lease liability at 2026-07-03 is therefore excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest 8.8 at 2026-07-03 (UV Smart majority stake) is deducted in the equity bridge; the flows are whole-company, so the NCI is charged once, in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: US operating company, industrial technology). No prior DCF; fresh build. BASIS: everything is continuing operations on the post-Ralliant (2025-06-28) portfolio. FY0 = FY2025 continuing revenue 4,159.1; reported_fcf = OperatingCashFlowContinuing 1,035.7 (kpis / 10-K FY2025) less an estimated 85 of continuing capex (whole-company capex 105.1 includes Ralliant H1-2025; H2-2025 continuing capex was 41.7 and H1-2026 was 54.7, so ~85 is the FY2025 continuing figure); owner FCF = 950.7 - 95 SBC - 0 interest income = 855.7 (levered, memo only -- the engine builds unlevered owner FCF from components and deducts net debt). Interest income is not stripped: cash of 374 is a fraction of the FCF base and the company is a net borrower. DEBT: the CSV TotalDebt column (FY2024 4,083.5, FY2025 4,105.5, 'Q2 2026' 4,388.9) double-counts the current portion -- XBRL LongTermDebt (total incl. current) is 3,707.3 / 3,206.0 / 3,489.1 and LongTermDebtCurrent is 376.2 / 899.5 / 899.8, and the CSV equals their sum. The DCF uses 3,509.3 from the 2026-07-03 balance sheet (all non-current after the Q2 refinancing of the 899.8 commercial paper). Also note the CSV row labelled 'Q2 2026' is the quarter ended 2026-04-03 (Fortive's Q1 2026); the true Q2 2026 (ended 2026-07-03, filed 2026-07-29) is not yet in the CSV and its anchors were read from the iXBRL directly. MARGINS: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC (the engine deducts SBC separately). FY2025 continuing GAAP EBITDA 1,157.8 (27.8%) + ~95 SBC = 30.1% pre-SBC; H1-2026 op income 401.6 + D&A 227.1 + SBC 45.2 = 673.9 on 2,166.2 = 31.1%. D&A is 10.5% of revenue but 368 of the 437.6 is acquired-intangible amortisation, which rolls off; da_pct_path declines to 7% so the tax shield is not perpetuated. TAX: FY2025 cash taxes paid 100 on 602 continuing pre-tax (16.6%; GAAP ETR 11.5% flattered by spin-related items); H1-2026 GAAP ETR 14.4%. The cash rate ramps 16% -> 20% on unlevered EBIT. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables + inventory exceed payables + deferred revenue growth, so growth consumes cash: wc_capture -8% of the revenue change. GUIDANCE ANCHOR: FY2026 revenue ~4.35B (+4.6%), core growth ~4%, adjusted EPS 2.95-3.05, 50-100bp annual adjusted-EBITDA-margin expansion framework (raised 2026-07-29 / Analysis.json). HISTORY: three portfolio separations (A&S sale 2018, Vontier 2020-21, Ralliant 2025) mean no multi-year CAGR is like-for-like; only FY2023-FY2025 continuing rows are comparable.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 core revenue growth guidance (~4%, raised from 2-3% on 2026-07-29), cross-checked against the FY2023-FY2025 continuing-operations revenue CAGR of 3.1% and H1-2026 reported growth of +7.8% (FX and UV Smart assisted).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Multi-year CAGRs are deliberately NOT computed: FY2014-17 revenue includes the 2018-divested Automation & Specialty businesses and Vontier, FY2019-22 includes Vontier through 2020 and Ralliant throughout, FY2023+ is continuing-only (ex-Ralliant). Equity fell 10,195.6 -> 6,461.1 in FY2025 on the spin distribution and 1,610.1 of buybacks, so book-value CAGR describes the separation, not compounding. The continuing 2-yr figures above are the only like-for-like series: revenue 3,913.9 -> 4,159.1 (3.1%); EPS continuing diluted 1.15 -> 1.59 (17.6%, buyback- and margin-aided from a spin-cost-depressed FY2023); owner FCF continuing ~678 (OCF 833.4 - ~70 capex - ~85 SBC) -> ~856 (12.4%).
historical_growth.notes: Selected 4.0% is a near-term anchor, not a long-run rate; the base path decelerates to 2.5% terminal. Owner-FCF CAGR (12.4%) exceeds revenue CAGR because FY2023 continuing OCF was depressed by separation costs and working capital; SBC has been flat-to-down as a share of revenue post-spin, so the SBC drag on reported FCF is not growing.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance (4.35B, +4.6%), then core growth of 4-4.5% fades to 2.5% by year 10 as Fluke data-center and recurring-revenue tailwinds mature. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands ~40bp/yr from 31.2% to 33.5% -- below management's 50-100bp framework because AHS mix is compressing and the standalone cost base is unproven. Cash tax ramps 16% -> 20% as spin-related benefits lapse. Intangible amortisation rolls off (D&A 10.5% -> 7%). Terminal 2.5% growth, 18x owner-FCF cap for a moderately cyclical industrial.

bull.narrative: Fluke's data-center test portfolio (CertiFiber Max) and double-digit recurring-revenue growth lift core growth to 6-6.5% in 2027-28 before fading to 3%; Gordian Flash AI and the workflow-software suite gain pricing power; management delivers the top of its 50-100bp margin framework, taking the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 36% by year 8. Terminal growth 3.0%, same 18x cap.

bear.narrative: FY2026 comes in slightly under guidance, then an industrial-capex downturn in 2027-28 (European softness becomes a demand contraction, China weak, tariff costs) takes revenue to 0% and -3% with negative operating leverage on the smaller post-spin cost base: pre-SBC EBITDA margin troughs at 28% and recovers only to 29.5%. AHS margin compression persists. Growth recovers to a 2-3% rate and terminal 2% at a 15x cap, reflecting a business the market treats as a mature hardware-heavy industrial rather than a software compounder.

scenario_narratives.base: Post-spin Fortive as a mid-single-digit grower with steady, below-framework margin expansion: FY2026 on the raised guidance (4.35B revenue, ~4% core, adjusted EPS 2.95-3.05), 4-4.5% growth through 2028 fading to 2.5%, pre-SBC EBITDA margin 31.2% -> 33.5%, cash tax normalising to 20%, intangible amortisation rolling off. Buybacks keep the diluted count flat while SBC (~2.2% of revenue) is expensed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-center test demand and Fluke recurring bundles, plus AI-enabled software (Gordian Flash AI, Intelex/Accruent) push growth to 6-6.5% in 2027-28 and management delivers the top of its 50-100bp margin framework (36% pre-SBC by year 8). A leaner, higher-recurring portfolio re-rates toward Roper-style multiples; terminal 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: An industrial-capex recession in 2027-28 (revenue 0% then -3%) hits the cyclical iOS hardware half while AHS mix keeps compressing; margins trough at 28% and never regain the FY2026 level; the untested standalone cost structure and 2.6x leverage limit the response. Terminal 2% at a 15x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: roughly half of revenue (Fluke, industrial software) follows the industrial capex cycle, Europe and China are already soft, and the standalone cost base and 2.6x net debt/EBITDA have not been through a downturn. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs data-center Fluke demand, AI software pricing and the top of the margin framework to land together, under a CEO one year into the job. Base 55% carries the raised FY2026 guidance and the consistent H1-2026 delivery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the continuing post-Ralliant business only, on unlevered owner FCF built from components (pre-SBC EBITDA, SBC expensed, rolling-off amortisation, cash tax ramping to 20%, growth-consuming working capital), discounted at an 8.5% USD WACC with net debt from the latest (2026-07-03) balance sheet and a flat fully diluted count. Pre-2023 history is treated as evidence of the Fluke/ASP moat and of cyclicality, not as a growth base, because the portfolio has been separated three times.
key_risks_to_valuation: Industrial capex cyclicality in the iOS segment (Fluke, industrial software) -- European softness and China weakness could become a revenue contraction rather than channel destocking
AHS margin compression from product mix and investment spend persisting beyond FY2026
Post-spin standalone cost structure and 2.6x net debt/EBITDA untested through a full cycle; refinancing at higher rates
Margin framework (50-100bp/yr) not delivered; base assumes ~40bp/yr, bull the top of the range
FX: ~half of revenue is non-USD (EUR, CNY); FY2026 guidance includes an FX tailwind
Capital allocation: bolt-on M&A (UV Smart) outside the organic model; acquisitions at high multiples would dilute the owner-FCF return
Terminal value is a large share of EV at an 8.5% WACC; the 18x cap and 2.5% terminal growth are the load-bearing assumptions
